28 Electromagnetic waves of equal wavelengths are emitted from two sources, X and Y. The waves
are emitted from X and Y with a phase difference of 180°.
A detector moves along a path that is parallel to the line XY and detects a pattern of intensity
maxima and minima.
The diagram shows the arrangement of the sources and the path of the detector.
X
Y
110 cm
path of detector
70 cm
Z
An intensity maximum is detected at point Z. Length XZ is 70 cm and length YZ is 110 cm.
What is a possible wavelength of the waves?
A
10 cm
B
16 cm
C
20 cm
D
40 cm

hints: Notice the distances $XZ = 70\text{ cm}$ and $YZ = 110\text{ cm}$ at point Z, so calculate the path difference $YZ - XZ$.
Remember the sources X and Y start $180^{\circ}$ out of phase, equal to half a wavelength, so the path must supply an extra half wavelength to get back in phase.
For a maximum the path difference must therefore equal a half-integer number of wavelengths: $40\text{ cm} = (n+0.5)\lambda$. Test which wavelength gives $2.5$, $1.5$, etc.
walkthrough: Calculate the path difference at Z: $YZ - XZ = 110\text{ cm} - 70\text{ cm} = 40\text{ cm}$. This is the extra distance the wave from Y travels.
State the condition for a maximum. Constructive interference needs total phase difference $0$, $360^{\circ}$, $720^{\circ}$, etc. at the detector.
Include the source phase. X and Y are emitted $180^{\circ}$ apart, so the path must contribute an odd multiple of $180^{\circ}$, i.e. a half-integer number of wavelengths.
Write the condition: path difference $= (n + 0.5)\lambda$ where $n = 0, 1, 2, ...$. So $40\text{ cm} = (n+0.5)\lambda$.
Test the options. Only $\lambda = 16\text{ cm}$ gives $40/16 = 2.5 = 2 + 0.5$, satisfying the condition with $n = 2$.
The other values give whole numbers: $40/10 = 4$, $40/20 = 2$, $40/40 = 1$, which with the $180^{\circ}$ start would give minima. This is option B.

A.explanation: With $\lambda = 10\text{ cm}$, $40\text{ cm}$ is $4\lambda$. The path gives in-phase arrival but the $180^{\circ}$ source shift then gives cancellation, so a minimum not a maximum.

B.explanation: With $\lambda = 16\text{ cm}$, $40\text{ cm}$ is $2.5\lambda$. The half-integer path shift cancels the $180^{\circ}$ source shift to give constructive interference.

C.explanation: With $\lambda = 20\text{ cm}$, $40\text{ cm}$ is $2\lambda$. The waves arrive in step from path alone, so the $180^{\circ}$ source difference makes them cancel.

D.explanation: With $\lambda = 40\text{ cm}$, $40\text{ cm}$ is $1\lambda$. Again the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths, so the $180^{\circ}$ source difference gives destructive interference.
